'''Ōka-no-Kuni-no-Atai''' (''ōka-no-kuni-no-atai''; dates of birth and death unknown) was a {{ill|gōzoku|ja|豪族}} of the {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}} and one of the '''{{ill|Kukuma no Kuni no Miyatsuko|ja|菊麻国造}}'''.

== Overview ==
In the "Kokuzō Hongi" of the ''{{ill|Sendai Kuji Hongi|ja|先代旧事本紀}}'', he is recorded as a son of {{ill|Etamohi-no-Mikoto|ja|兄多毛比命}}, ancestor of the {{ill|Musashi no Kuni no Miyatsuko|ja|武蔵国造}}, and is said to have been appointed Kukuma no Kuni no Miyatsuko (''kukuma no kuni no miyatsuko'') during the reign of {{ill|Emperor Seimu|ja|成務天皇}}.

{{ill|Hōga Toshio|ja|宝賀寿男}} argues that, because the ancestors of the Ise-Ōka-no-Obito were also connected to {{ill|Hitachi Province|ja|常陸国}} in the eastern provinces, there was a connection through the female line. He also argues that Ōka-no-Kuni-no-Atai's daughter Otohime became consort of {{ill|Emperor Chūai|ja|仲哀天皇}}, and that through this connection, the clan's {{ill|Isachi-no-Sukune|ja|海上五十狭茅|lt=Isachi-no-Sukune|lt_ja=五十狭茅宿禰}} sided with {{ill|Prince Kagosaka|ja|麛坂皇子}} and {{ill|Prince Oshikuma|ja|忍熊皇子}}.<ref name="houga" />

A tradition holds that his tomb is in Myōkō Village in {{ill|Ichihara District|ja|市原郡}}, and that his son was Oka-no-Atai.<ref>{{ill|Ōta Akira|ja|太田亮}}, "Kukuma" in ''Seishi Kakei Daijiten'', p. 1869.</ref>
